::: {.lede}
I study how wildlife populations change over time, using long-term field data, telemetry, and camera traps, with a focus on wolves and white-tailed deer.
:::

I worked as a biotechnician with the U.S. Geological Survey Wolf and Deer Project in Ely, Minnesota, where I helped radio-track wolves and white-tailed deer in the Superior National Forest. My graduate research at the University of British Columbia Okanagan examines the drivers of white-tailed deer range expansion in the Columbia Mountains, and I also work on wildlife research with Swamp Donkey Solutions in British Columbia.

## Current work

- **[Wolf pup survival in northeastern Minnesota](projects/snf-wolf-pups/index.qmd).** How long radio-collared wolf pups survived, what killed them, and why, from five decades of telemetry data. Presented at the International Wolf Symposium, 2026.
- **[White-tailed deer range expansion](research.qmd#white-tailed-deer).** What is driving white-tailed deer into the Columbia Mountains of British Columbia.
